text:
Ivy: uploaded a tiny experiment for compact latency rows — figma: https://www.figma.com/file/compact-experiment (frame: compact-inline-sampler). Need quick takes on: where to show sample count, preset behavior when switching ranges, minimal copy for sampler, and a11y focus behavior.

Sam: nice. For sample count: prefer an inline `n=` micro-pill inside the metric chip. collapses on small widths.

Ravi: buckets: don't shift bucket bins on zoom — fixed buckets by default. adaptive can be an opt-in in panel settings.

Maya: motion: use immediate switch for big range jumps (>24h) and short 120ms crossfade for small changes. also respect prefers-reduced-motion.

Ivy: copy choices: `Sampling granularity` vs `Sampling`. Which is clearer?

Sam: `Sampling granularity` is clearer; pair with tooltip: "Higher granularity increases accuracy and compute." Keep tooltip <80 chars.

Ravi: keyboard: make cells focusable and arrow-key navigable. on focus announce `95th percentile: 320 ms; sample size: 23; sampled`. Also add focus ring that doesn't obscure neighbors.

DesignerBot: a11y scan: contrast checks ok for micro-pill at 12px; recommend aria-live polite for sampling updates and explicit aria-labels for presets.

Maya: UX decision proposal: inline `n=` pill (hide on tiny widths), fixed buckets default, crossfade <24h else instant, label `Sampling granularity` + short tooltip, focusable cells with SR announcement.

Ivy: perfect — i'll update figma and post v2. Thanks! :thumbsup:
